unit_description: This unit extends place-value understanding to numbers through 100,000. Students read, write, build, and compare larger numbers, and use place-value thinking to solve number puzzles.
unit_goals: Understand the thousands and ten-thousands places.
Write large numbers in standard, expanded, and word form.
Use place-value reasoning to solve number puzzles.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students explore numbers through 100,000 by reading, building, writing, and solving place-value puzzles with larger numbers.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by counting by thousands: 1,000, 2,000, 3,000, ...
lessons.concept: A five-digit number has ten-thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones places. In 45,218, the 4 means 40,000.
lessons.practice: Name the value of each digit in numbers through 100,000.
lessons.objective: Understand the value of each digit in numbers through 100,000.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by naming the value of the underlined digit.

questions.prompt: In 23__,456__, what is the value of the underlined digits?
questions.hint: The 3 is in the ten-thousands place.

questions.prompt: In 7__1__,029, what is the value of the underlined digit?
questions.hint: The 1 is in the thousands place.

learn.title: Thousands and Ten-Thousands
teaching_points: A five-digit number has a ten-thousands place.
A six-digit number has a hundred-thousands place.
Each place is ten times larger than the place to its right.

example.prompt: In 67,892, what does the 6 stand for?
example.equation: 6 is in the ten-thousands place, so it means 60,000.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.hint: The 8 is in the ten-thousands place.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Name the value of each underlined digit in numbers through 100,000.

flashcards.title: Large Number Places
flashcards.instructions: Review place-value words for large numbers.

bigIdea.title: Thousands and Ten-Thousands
bigIdea.subtitle: Bigger numbers have more places
bigIdea.intro: Numbers can have five or six digits. The place farthest to the left always tells us how big the number is.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How does each place get ten times larger?

ruleCards.description: The digit in the ten-thousands place is worth ten times as much as the same digit in the thousands place.
The digit in the thousands place is worth ten times as much as the same digit in the hundreds place.

lessons.fact_drill: Quickly read numbers shown on a place-value chart.
lessons.concept: Read large numbers from left to right, naming each period. The number 56,789 is read as fifty-six thousand, seven hundred eighty-nine.
lessons.practice: Match written numbers to digits and read numbers aloud.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by reading these numbers.

questions.hint: Say the thousands period, then the rest.

questions.prompt: Write 'eighty-two thousand, one hundred nineteen' as digits.

questions.hint: Six digits: 1 followed by five zeros.

learn.title: Read and Identify Numbers Through 100,000
teaching_points: Use a comma to separate the thousands period.
Read the rest of the number like a three-digit number.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Write the number in words, or write the word name as digits.

flashcards.title: Reading Large Numbers
flashcards.instructions: Practice reading and writing numbers through 100,000.

bigIdea.title: Read and Identify Numbers Through 100,000
bigIdea.subtitle: Use commas and periods to read big numbers
bigIdea.intro: Big numbers are easier to read when you break them into periods. Read the thousands period first, then the rest.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why is the comma helpful when reading numbers?

ruleCards.description: Read the thousands period first, then the rest of the number.
Zeros keep a digit in the correct place, but we don't say them when reading.

lessons.fact_drill: Write three large numbers in expanded form as a warm-up.
lessons.concept: Expanded form for large numbers adds the value of each digit. 45,218 = 40,000 + 5,000 + 200 + 10 + 8.
lessons.practice: Convert between standard and expanded form for numbers through 100,000.
lessons.objective: Write numbers through 100,000 in expanded form.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by breaking numbers into parts.

questions.prompt: What is the value of 8 in 86,341?
questions.hint: The 8 is in the ten-thousands place.

learn.title: Expanded Form Through 100,000
teaching_points: Write each digit with its place value.
Skip the digit if it is a zero.
Add the parts together to get the number.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Switch numbers between standard and expanded form through 100,000.

flashcards.title: Expanded Form Large Numbers
flashcards.instructions: Match standard and expanded forms of large numbers.

bigIdea.title: Expanded Form Through 100,000
bigIdea.subtitle: Break big numbers into their parts
bigIdea.intro: Large numbers are made of ten-thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones. Expanded form shows every part.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How does expanded form help us understand big numbers?

ruleCards.description: When a digit is zero, we skip that part in expanded form.
A 1 in the hundred-thousands place means one hundred thousand.

lessons.fact_drill: Quickly identify the mystery digit from clues about its place value.
lessons.concept: Use what you know about place value to solve puzzles. If a number has 6 ten-thousands, 3 hundreds, and 5 ones, the number is 60,305.
lessons.practice: Solve place-value riddles and build numbers from clues.
lessons.objective: Use place-value clues to build and name numbers.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by solving place-value riddles.

questions.prompt: I have 4 ten-thousands, 2 hundreds, and 7 ones. What number am I?
What is the largest four-digit number?
Which digit is in the thousands place in 28,413?
questions.hint: Count three places from the right.

learn.title: Number Names and Place-Value Puzzles
teaching_points: Write each digit in the correct place.
Use zeros to hold empty places.

example.prompt: Build the number with 7 ten-thousands, 0 thousands, 4 hundreds, and 9 ones.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Build the number with 5 ten-thousands, 3 thousands, 0 hundreds, 2 tens, and 8 ones.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Solve the place-value riddles by building the mystery number.

flashcards.title: Place-Value Clues
flashcards.instructions: Review vocabulary for solving place-value puzzles.

bigIdea.title: Number Names and Place-Value Puzzles
bigIdea.subtitle: Use clues to build numbers
bigIdea.intro: A place-value puzzle gives you clues about each digit. Use a place-value chart to put every digit in the right spot.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How can clues help you build a number?

ruleCards.description: Zeros keep the other digits in the correct places.
Each clue tells you how many of that place-value group there are.

lessons.fact_drill: Rapid review of digit values, reading, expanded form, and number puzzles.
lessons.concept: Review the big ideas from this unit: thousands, ten-thousands, reading, writing, expanded form, and number puzzles.
lessons.practice: Complete a balanced evaluation covering the skills from this unit.
lessons.objective: Show what you know about numbers through 100,000.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Get ready to show what you know.

questions.prompt: What is the value of 6 in 64,719?
questions.hint: The 6 is in the ten-thousands place.

learn.title: Ready to Show What You Know
teaching_points: Use a place-value chart if you get stuck.

example.prompt: You have learned four big ideas this unit.
example.equation: large digits + reading numbers + expanded form + place-value puzzles = numbers through 100,000

practice_block.title: Unit Evaluation
practice_block.instructions: Answer all questions carefully to show your understanding.

flashcards.title: Unit 2 Review
flashcards.instructions: Review key terms from Unit 2 before the evaluation.

bigIdea.title: Unit Evaluation: Numbers Through 100,000
bigIdea.subtitle: Show what you know
bigIdea.intro: This evaluation checks your understanding of the four big ideas from this unit: thousands, ten-thousands, reading large numbers, expanded form, and number puzzles.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you know about numbers through 100,000?

ruleCards.equation: A digit's place tells its value
ruleCards.description: Remember that the same digit can mean different amounts depending on its place.
The same number can be written in standard form, expanded form, or words.
